claims.claim: Standard C Richter layout: blow notes holes 1-10 are C E G C E G C E G C (C4 E4 G4 C5 E5 G5 C6 E6 G6 C7); draw notes are D G B D F A B D F A (D4 G4 B4 D5 F5 A5 B5 D6 F6 A6). Draw is higher than blow in holes 1-6, blow is higher than draw in holes 7-10 (hole 7: blow C6, draw B5).

claims.notes: The note letters come from a search summary; octave numbers (C4 start) are from the standard convention and my own working, not from a page. The Wikipedia 'Richter tuning' example table (C E G C D F A C E A) is not the standard layout and must not be used. Two vendor/teaching pages are not independent enough to count as corroboration at Tier 1.

claims.claim: Other keys are the C layout transposed by a constant interval. Hole 4 on a standard G harmonica (hole 1 blow G3) is G4 blow and A4 draw, which is the C-harp hole 4 pair (C5, D5) lowered by 5 semitones. The input file's example is correct for a standard G harp; a 'low G' harp (hole 1 blow G2) would be an octave lower.
claims.input_file_says: hole 4 on a G harmonica pairs a G4 blow reed with an A4 draw reed
claims.notes: Derived by transposition from B7 and the convention that a G harp starts at G3. The G3 start was not checked on a page; it is a standard convention but a design should make the lowest note a parameter.

claims.claim: Bend sizes on a C harp (standard practice, unverified here): draw bends in holes 1 (1 semitone), 2 (2), 3 (3), 4 (1), 5 (about a semitone or less, since draw F5 is only one semitone above blow E5), 6 (1); blow bends in holes 8 (1), 9 (1), 10 (up to 2). Hole 7 has no usable bend. Each bend stops just above the pitch of the lower reed in that hole, so the maximum bend is bounded by the interval between the two reeds (hole 3 draw B4 down to G4 blow: 4 semitones apart, 3 bend steps).

claims.notes: Search summaries disagreed on which holes bend (one said 1, 4, 6 only, another said 1-4, 6 draw and 8-10 blow). The sizes above are from the interval between the two reeds in B7 plus common teaching practice and must be checked against a source before use. The interval bound is the important design rule.

claims.claim: Overblow notes on a C harp sound about a semitone above the draw reed's note: 1OB Eb4, 4OB Eb5, 5OB F#5, 6OB Bb5 (2OB and 3OB duplicate other notes). Overdraws sound about a semitone above the blow reed's note: 7OD C#6, 9OD Ab6, 10OD Db7 (8OD duplicates F6). A source lists the practically used ones as overblows Eb, F#, Bb and overdraws Db, Ab, C#.

claims.claim: Mechanism claimed in the harmonica literature (Johnston 1987; Bahnson et al. 1998): in a draw bend the higher (draw) reed's frequency is lowered by vocal-tract coupling while the lower (blow) reed behaves as an opening reed and takes over; in an overblow or overdraw the originally driven reed is choked and the other reed speaks, about a semitone above its rest pitch. This was NOT confirmed from the primary texts in this round.

claims.claim: The real-time MRI harmonica bending study is by Peter R. Egbert (Stanford, ophthalmology), Thomas D. Rossing, David Barrett and Lewis Shin, with Andrew Holbrook named on Barrett's site. It imaged a professional player on non-magnetic harmonicas, with 3-D static and 2-D real-time upper-airway images of unbent and bent notes. Barrett's site reports that the anterior chamber (tongue hump to harmonica) controls bend depth, and deeper bends move the constriction backwards, with a scooped tongue shape for the deepest bends.

claims.claim: Half-valving puts windsavers on the draw reeds of holes 1-6 and the blow reeds of holes 7-10 (the higher-pitched reed in each hole, 10 of 20 reeds); these reeds then bend as single reeds (no cooperation from the opposite reed), and valved bends are reported to reach at least a semitone, with most players managing a whole tone. Valves block overblows and overdraws.

summary:
Only web search worked, and only as snippets; web fetch and curl could not reach external hosts, so no primary text was read and nothing is Tier-1 verified.
Bahnson et al. (JASA 103(4), 1998), Johnston (Acoustics Australia 15, 1987) and Millot, Cuesta and Valette (Acta Acustica 87, 2001) exist; contents unread.
C Richter layout, G-harp hole 4 example (G4/A4, correct) and overblow/overdraw notes are consistent with the file; bend sizes inferred.
MRI study is Egbert, Rossing, Barrett, Shin (journal paper not found); no Forstch paper found; reed dimensions and plate sides unverified.
